name: Libni
title: Levitical clan founder
summary: Libni was a son of Gershon and a grandson of Levi, one of the twelve sons of Israel. He was the founder of the Libnite clan among the Levites, who were responsible for service at the tabernacle. His descendants played an important role in temple service throughout Israel's history.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as a son of Gershon
keyEvents.description: Libni is mentioned as the firstborn son of Gershon, son of Levi, in the genealogies.

keyEvents.title: The Libnite clan is established
keyEvents.description: Libni's descendants were registered as a distinct clan among the Gershonites, known as the Libnites.

keyEvents.title: The Tent Service of the Gershonites
keyEvents.description: The Libnites, as part of the Gershonites, were responsible for the tabernacle's curtains, coverings, and veils during the wilderness journey.

keyEvents.title: The Lineage of Libni in 1 Chronicles
keyEvents.description: The lineage of Libni is recorded in the Books of Chronicles as part of the Levitical genealogy, with his descendants serving in the temple.

keyEvents.title: The Camp of the Gershonites
keyEvents.description: The Libnites and the other Gershonites were assigned their camp behind the tabernacle, to the west, during the wilderness journey.
